components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Highest-priority action per view (hero CTA, Contact CTA).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 3px; background: #14213D; color: #F5F5F1; border: 1px solid #14213D; text-decoration: none; transition: background 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #223059; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #14213D; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action paired next to a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 3px; background: transparent; color: #14213D; border: 1px solid #B7B4A6; text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 160ms, background 160ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #14213D; background: #FBFBF9; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #14213D; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Project status indicator; live/shipped/wrapped are the only three variants.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 100px; border: 1px solid currentColor; color: #285F50; background: #C9DED7; } .ds-pill::before { content: '\25CF'; font-size: 0.6em; }

components.name: Spec Grid
components.description: Signature bordered data-table component; the single vocabulary for both hero quick-facts and animated career-stat counters. Do not create a separate stat-card pattern.
components.html: Based inPune, India
components.css: .ds-spec-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); border: 1px solid #D8D6CC; border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; background: #FBFBF9; } .ds-spec-cell { padding: 1.5rem; border-right: 1px solid #D8D6CC; } .ds-spec-label { display: block; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #5A6578; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; } .ds-spec-value { font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.1875rem; }

components.name: Card
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FBFBF9; border: 1px solid #D8D6CC; border-radius: 6px; padding: 2rem; transition: transform 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), border-color 380ms; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); border-color: #B7B4A6; } .ds-card h3 { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; } .ds-card p { color: #4A5268; }

components.css: .ds-preview-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; border: 1px solid #D8D6CC; border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; background: #FBFBF9; transition: transform 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 380ms; } .ds-preview-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 12px 24px -16px rgba(20,33,61,0.25); } .ds-preview-top { padding: 1.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #D8D6CC; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; } .ds-preview-body { padding: 1.5rem; flex: 1; } .ds-preview-foot { padding: 1rem 1.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #7A4D14; border-top: 1px solid #D8D6CC; }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Desktop primary nav with mono links, underline-wipe hover, and amber-deep active state.
components.html: HomeWorkAboutContact
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 2rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-nav a { position: relative; text-decoration: none; color: #14213D; padding-block: 0.25rem; } .ds-nav a::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 100%; bottom: -2px; height: 1.5px; background: #C98A2C; transition: right 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-nav a:hover::after, .ds-nav a:focus-visible::after, .ds-nav a[aria-current='page']::after { right: 0; } .ds-nav a[aria-current='page'] { color: #7A4D14; }

narrative.overview:
The site treats a career as a versioned, statused product document rather than a portfolio brochure. Every page opens as if a file had been opened, not a landing page loaded: a metadata strip (FILE:, STATUS:, LAST UPDATED:) sits above the nav on every page, status pills (Live / Shipped / Wrapped) and version tags (v7.0, v6.0...) recur throughout, and numeric facts are laid out in a bordered mono spec-grid rather than as marketing stat cards. This direction was fixed by the project's own PRD (PRODUCT.md, Positioning section) before the build started — it is a brief-pinned world, not one arrived at through a concept-seed tournament, and the tokens/type/rejections below were set by that brief rather than discovered through exploration.

The palette is paper-and-ink: a warm off-white ground, near-navy ink for text, and two accent hues (amber, teal) reserved for status signaling — never for large fields of color or for direct body text. The system reads as restrained and document-like at rest, with warmth supplied by the fluid type scale, the 1.65 body line-height, and first-person case-study copy rather than by decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground + ink type + hairline rules, styled like an opened document, not a marketing page.
IBM Plex Mono reserved for all metadata (labels, dates, tags, status text); Space Grotesk for headings; Inter for reading copy.
Amber and teal are structural/status accents only; a separate 'deep' variant of each exists specifically so they can appear as text.
Motion is additive only — every animated system (reveal, count-up, progress rail) ships a fully visible, fully functional zero-JS baseline first.
Exactly one numeric-data visual vocabulary (the bordered spec-grid) is reused for both the hero's quick-facts and the animated career stats.

rules.name: The Deep-Variant-For-Text Rule
rules.body: amber and teal are reserved for backgrounds, borders, dots, and gradient fills — never for direct text color on a light surface. Any time amber or teal family color needs to render as legible text, use amber-deep or teal-deep instead. This split exists because the base hues failed WCAG contrast on paper during finish review; reintroducing base-hue text would reintroduce that failure.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Metadata Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is used exclusively for data/label/status content (dates, tags, labels, counters, nav links) — never for headings or reading prose. If a piece of text is 'information about the page' rather than 'the page's content,' it renders in mono.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat and bordered at rest. A shadow may appear only as a hover-state response on an interactive card; it must never be a resting-state property of any surface.

dos: Do reserve IBM Plex Mono for metadata/labels/status content only (see The Mono-Is-Metadata Rule).
Do use amber-deep/teal-deep for any accent-family text on a light surface; use base amber/teal only for backgrounds, borders, dots, and the progress-rail gradient (The Deep-Variant-For-Text Rule).
Do route any new numeric/stat callout through the existing .spec-grid component rather than building a new stat-card pattern.

Do ship every motion-based feature (reveal-on-scroll, count-up, etc.) with a fully visible, fully functional CSS-only baseline that requires no JS, matching prefers-reduced-motion behavior already established for reveal, count-up, and magnetic hover.

Do preserve the triple-redundant trigger pattern (IntersectionObserver + manual scroll/resize bounding-rect check + ~2500ms hard timeout fallback) in any future reveal or count-up work; do not simplify it back to IO-only. This exists because a prior build of this exact site shipped content that stayed permanently invisible when IO never fired in a static-rendering context.
Do keep dashed borders limited to the two 'not-final/placeholder' signals (PAO-grid rule, visual-placeholder tile).
donts: Don't add a decorative eyebrow/kicker line above headings. An earlier version of the hero had one; it was removed site-wide during finish review as an unconditional anti-pattern. (A .hero__eyebrow style still exists in css/main.css but is unused by any page — it is dead CSS from that removal, not a component to reinstate or reference.)
Don't use base amber or teal as a direct text color on paper, paper-raised, or paper-sunken — it fails contrast; use the -deep variant.
Don't add a fourth status-pill variant without a real corresponding project status; the three (live/shipped/wrapped) map to actual case-study states, not decorative options.
Don't introduce a resting-state box-shadow on any card, button, or container; shadow is reserved for the one hover-interaction case on preview cards.
